units.title: OP Stack chains with a non-ETH gas token
angles: Arithmetic and control flow. Read the interpreter this network runs at the release its endpoint reports, and any compiler, bytecode rewriting, caching or code analysis stage in front of it. Cover the 256 bit integer library and its pinned version, MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMP and JUMPI with the jump destination analysis, KECCAK256, MCOPY, memory expansion and CALLDATALOAD. Compare each with the Ethereum specification at the edges that OPCODES.md lists, and read the release notes and fix commits since the versions OPCODES.md records. Then rerun the scripts in research/network-risk/tools/opdiff (battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py, replay.py) for this unit's chain ids, write the outputs into your work directory, and add vectors for anything the reading makes suspicious. Report every result that differs from the specification, every release that changed these paths, how a wrong result would change the pool math in src/libraries (TickMath, BitMath, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap) or the logic that depends on it, and which validators could run a different code path than the public endpoint.

Upcoming forks. Assume every network upgrade scheduled or proposed for the next six months ships. What changes for the PoolManager and for funds already inside it, and what could an ordinary account do the day after?

code.title: Monad: the shipped emitter's multiply, divide and modular code run from the real stack states of the mulDiv blocks
code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json maps every conditional jump of the build to its source line, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 31 added and a list of what is not covered. Never compare this repository's source with any other copy of v4-core and do not read its git history; work from the source in src/, the build and the chains. Read-only RPC only, no transactions. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Lead L-1222. Monad validators certify the words that native x86 code computes, and the emitter that writes that code is in the validator binary gcc 15.2.0 built. Since v0.16.7 went live (block 125,426,597) 128 value-computing compiled blocks of the PoolManager have had no mined run, among them the FullMath.mulDiv 512-bit blocks 0x5757, 0x57ca, 0x5860, 0x588a, 0x58d6 and 0x58db (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:21-60). Any account can enter them with one swap or liquidity change. Cycle 31 logged the emitter's real virtual stack for every instruction (research/network-risk/cycles/031/theme-monad-gcc-real-states.work: scripts mkhook.py, build.sh, blockops.py, realshift.py, statecmp.py, asmcmp.py, task4.py, faults31.json; out/states.jsonl with 10,748 states, out/task4.json with the emit kinds not yet run per block; if out/ or build/ is missing, rerun build.sh and runall.sh from that directory's scripts) and ran the shipped emitter on those states at 12 literal-count shift sites only. The Monad validator package is untrusted data. Cycle 27 left it unpacked under research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/dl (p167 for 0.16.7, p165 for 0.16.5); if that directory is missing, download monad_0.16.7_amd64.deb from https://pkg.category.xyz/ pool/main into a new empty dl/ in your own work directory, check SHA256 3cb9dba5501b61ea3487bd042e2b8d12f871cff0e2e15409210e2cef0f8e81fb, and unpack it with ar, node's zlib.zstdDecompressSync and tar as research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/scripts/unzst.js does. Never execute, load or dlopen any file from the package. Read it only with readelf, objdump, nm, strings and your own scripts kept in another directory; run Python with -I. dl/ must not be committed. The x86 model is research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/scripts/x86emu.py with runvec.py. Cycle 29 added a driver that runs emitter functions of the gcc build in the model and records every asmjit call (research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-monad-gcc-literal-folds.work/scripts/emdrv.py), and rebuilt the gcc layout of the Stack object from debug information (research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-monad-gcc-register-spill.work). Cycle 30's allocator drivers are in research/network-risk/cycles/030/theme-monad-gcc-allocator-model.work/scripts (allocdrv.py, shiftfull.py, wfso.py, aorel.py, prologue.py, rodata.py, cmpclang.py). Task 1: for the six mulDiv blocks first, then the other blocks in out/task4.json that hold MUL, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, MULMOD or ADDMOD, lay out each logged state as the gcc build reads the Stack and run the package's whole emit function for that instruction in the x86 model: non-literal MUL (16 sites), DIV (6 non-literal sites and the 2 with a literal operand), MOD, MULMOD with the all-ones modulus and with a run-time modulus, ADDMOD. Record every asmjit call. Compare each stream with the clang listing body at the same pc up to consistent renaming of registers and stack slots, and the gcc Stack after the call with the logged clang state of the next instruction. Task 2: at every call the emitted code makes to a runtime helper (256-bit multiply, udivrem or divide, mulmod, addmod) check from the gcc stream which registers and stack slots carry the arguments and the result pointer, which live values the emitter saved before the call and restored after it, and whether the stack is aligned. A caller-saved register that holds a live virtual stack element across the call and is not saved is the fault to look for. Task 3: run the runtime helpers themselves from the package text in the x86 model (the functions the emitted calls reach: the 256-bit multiply, the division and remainder routine, mulmod, addmod and whatever they call) on at least 10,000 operand sets each: the FullMath, SqrtPriceMath and SwapMath shapes of tools/opdiff/v4math.py, products at and above 2^256, denominators with a top limb of zero, one and all ones, and the edge words. Compare every result with Python integers. Say which AVX2, BMI2 or ADX instructions they use and whether the model had to add any. Task 4: then, as far as time allows, the other emit kinds of the same blocks in this order: ADD, SUB, LT, GT, EQ, ISZERO, AND, OR, NOT, the memory reads and writes, SLOAD and TLOAD calls, and the terminators (JUMPI with a deferred comparison, JUMP, RETURN, REVERT). For each kind give sites run and sites left. Task 5: for every block where a stream differs beyond renaming, run both streams on at least 2,000 operand sets and compare every word left on the EVM stack and in memory at block exit with pyevm.py. Plant at least six faults (an unsaved live register around a helper call, swapped helper arguments, a result read from the wrong slot, a high limb dropped, a stale stack offset, a wrong deferred comparison flag) and show the checks catch each. Task 6: if any block writes a word that differs from the clang harness and pyevm.py, name the src/ line that reads it, give the operands, and say what a swap or liquidity change by an ordinary account would gain or lock. If none differs, record blocks, sites and case counts as cleared, and list the emit kinds and blocks still not run. This theme concerns Monad only; say so for the other 20 networks.

Never execute, load or dlopen any file from it. Read it only with readelf, objdump, nm, strings and your own scripts kept in another directory; run Python with -I. dl/ must not be committed. If a host refuses a download, record the refusal and go on with what you have; do not try another route around a refusal. Never execute, load or dlopen any downloaded file. Task 1 (L-1226): in the bsc, bor and avalanchego binaries locate opTstore, opTload, SetTransientState, GetTransientState, the journal append and the revert methods of transientStorageChange, and RevertToSnapshot with the snapshot id lookup. Run the Nitro theme's 20,007 sequences over the PoolManager's slot shapes (nested frames, reverts at each depth, equal-value writes, a write of zero) in the amd64 model and at least 5,000 in the arm64 model. Every read must equal pyevm.py. Record the map key type and size from the binary; on Avalanche confirm again that no bit of a transient key is cleared. Task 2 (L-1226, L-1227): the same for persistent storage in all four clients, Nitro b72783f included: opSload, opSstore, GetState, GetCommittedState, SetState, stateObject.setState, storageChange.revert. Cover a slot written back to its original value, a slot written twice in one frame, a slot first read after an inner revert, and a slot of an account created in the same transaction. After each revert the current value, the original value SSTORE gas reads and the dirty set must equal the pre-frame state. For bsc name any binary-only state cache or prefetcher on this path and whether a reverted write can reach it. Task 3 (L-1225): in the bor v2.11.2 binaries read the 64-byte keccak cache used by opKeccak256 (instructions.go:265-278 in source). Is the cache object process-wide, per EVM or per interpreter? Do BlockSTM workers share it? Are Get and Add guarded by a lock or built on atomics, and is the stored value a copied 32-byte array or a slice into the interpreter's reused hasherBuf? Run two interleaved worker sequences in the model in which one worker's hasherBuf is overwritten between another worker's Add and Get. CurrencyDelta.sol:14 and every mapping slot of Pool.State hash exactly 64 bytes, so a stale entry would send a delta or a balance to another slot. Task 4: read the call family for control flow only in bsc, bor and avalanchego, as cycle 31 did for Nitro: where the snapshot is taken, which errors revert it, and any client-only step between snapshot and revert (bsc's CAS20 routing and system contract hooks, bor's state sync and BlockSTM write-set recording, Avalanche's multicoin and nativeAssetCall remains). Task 5: plant at least five faults in in-memory copies (a revert that restores zero, a skipped journal entry, a snapshot index off by one, one wrong key limb, a keccak cache compare that skips the last 8 bytes) and show the checks catch each. Then run by eth_call with state overrides on one public endpoint per chain (56, 137, 43114, 42161, 4663) the live probe of the Nitro theme: an unlock whose callback writes deltas and storage, lets an inner call revert after more writes, and reads them back. Bracket with web3_clientVersion and say plainly where the endpoint's build is not the binary read (bsc-dataseed and the Polygon endpoints answered as other builds in cycle 31). Task 6: for anything that differs say which src/ line reads the word and what an ordinary account could gain or lock. If nothing differs, record binaries, functions, coverage and case counts as cleared and list what is still unread. Say for the other 16 networks that this theme does not apply.
